interpretation: This packet records first-party source observations for reviewer use. It does not approve the authority, opportunity, eligibility rule, benefit, window, or publication status.
sourcePolicy: The Ministry of Tourism NIDHI+ portal, its current guidelines index, the Common National Standards guideline and State/UT tourism authorities are primary. Central classification is kept separate from local licences, project approvals, construction permissions and commercial occupancy outcomes.

records.sourceAnchor: Common National Standards guideline pages 3-6: one to six rooms/up to 12 beds, owner/operator residence, inspection, two-year validity, Silver/Gold fees, documents and classification/reclassification route
observations: The Ministry guideline describes a classification and official listing route for eligible Bed & Breakfast and Homestay establishments, not a grant, loan, subsidy, guaranteed occupancy or replacement for local permissions.

A Homestay route requires the owner/promoter and family to physically reside in the establishment; the Bed & Breakfast route requires an owner-appointed agent or operator to reside on the premises. Both routes describe one to six lettable rooms and up to 12 beds.

The guideline requires inspection readiness and states two-year classification validity, with Silver and Gold classification/reclassification fees listed as INR 3,000 and INR 5,000 respectively; the live portal and applicable State/UT route must control current payment and renewal details.

NIDHI+ currently exposes unit registration and classification-related routes, while its current notice says fresh voluntary project-approval applications for hospitality units at the construction/pre-construction stage are not entertained from 16 March 2026 and pending applications were treated as closed.

The central guideline does not by itself replace municipal, fire, police, food, building, tax, labour, environmental or State/UT permissions. Changes, inspection deficiencies, validity, reclassification and withdrawal conditions must be tracked separately.
reviewFollowUps: Confirm whether the user's State/UT has its own controlling homestay or hospitality classification scheme and whether the Central route is applicable before recommending it.
Verify the current NIDHI+ registration flow, live fee screen, required uploads, regional classification authority, inspection checklist and two-year renewal/reclassification process.
Check owner/operator residence, room and bed count, ownership or lease evidence, police clearance, safety, hygiene, facility, photograph and undertaking requirements.
Explicitly block the discontinued construction/pre-construction project-approval route from recommendations and distinguish it from operational-unit registration/classification.
Track every State/UT and local licence independently; obtain an authorized reviewer decision before publishing any actionable classification recommendation.

publicationGuard.reason: The official guideline and NIDHI+ portal support a conditional operational-unit classification route, but State/UT applicability, current portal fields, fees, inspection, local permissions and the discontinued project-approval boundary require reviewer confirmation. The record remains review-gated.
